      25                         : // Our goal in this file is to convert a module in the Slang IR over to an
      26                         : // equivalent module in the SPIR-V intermediate language.
      27                         : //
      28                         : // The Slang IR is (intentionally) similar to SPIR-V in many ways, and both
      29                         : // can represent shaders at similar levels of abstraction, so much of the
      30                         : // translation involves one-to-one translation of Slang IR instructions
      31                         : // to their SPIR-V equivalents.
      32                         : //
      33                         : // SPIR-V differs from Slang IR in some key ways, and the SPIR-V
      34                         : // specification places many restrictions on how the IR can be encoded.
      35                         : // In some cases we will rely on earlier IR passes to convert Slang IR
      36                         : // into a form closer to what SPIR-V expects (e.g., by moving all
      37                         : // varying entry point parameters to global scope), but other differences
      38                         : // will be handled during the translation process.
      39                         : //
      40                         : // The logic in this file relies on the formal [SPIR-V Specification].
      41                         : // When we are making use of or enforcing some property from the spec,
      42                         : // we will try to refer to the relevant section in comments.
      43                         : //
      44                         : // [SPIR-V Specification]: https://www.khronos.org/registry/spir-v/specs/unified1/SPIRV.html
      45                         : 
      46                         : // [2.3: Physical Layout of a SPIR-V Module and Instruction]
      47                         : //
      48                         : // > A SPIR-V module is a single linear stream of words.
      49                         : 
      50                         : 
      51                         : // [2.3: Physical Layout of a SPIR-V Module and Instruction]
      52                         : //
      53                         : // > All remaining words are a linear sequence of instructions.
      54                         : // > Each instruction is a stream of words
      55                         : //
      56                         : // After a fixed-size header, the contents of a SPIR-V module
      57                         : // is just a flat sequence of instructions, each of which is
      58                         : // just a sequence of words.
      59                         : //

      62                         : // constraints placed by the SPIR-V encoding that would make

      67                         : // SPIR-V imposes some global ordering constraints on instructions,

      69                         : // For example, all `OpCapability` instructions must come before any

      99                         : // While the SPIR-V module is nominally (according to the spec) just

     101                         : // are logically in a parent/child relationship.

     104                         : // and the matching `OpFunctionEnd`. We can also think of basic
     105                         : // blocks within a function as owning the instructions between
     106                         : // an `OpLabel` (which represents the bloc) and the next label
     107                         : // or the end of the function.
     108                         : //
     109                         : // Furthermore, the common case is SPIR-V is that an instruction
     110                         : // that defines some value must appear before any instruction
     111                         : // that uses that value as an operand. This property is often true
